column1:
In addition to the FOMC’s clearly positive assessment (strong growth, tight labor market, inflation near 2%), the mid-2018 SLOOS adds that banks—especially foreign banks—eased C&I lending standards and narrowed loan rate spreads, citing a stronger economic outlook and labor market. That corroborates supportive credit conditions and reinforces the near-term positive tone. While some segments (e.g., certain consumer/CRE categories) were less uniformly easy, the balance of SLOOS evidence tilts toward easier credit supply rather than tightening.

Net effect: relative to the earlier FSR-based caution, SLOOS points to more accommodative credit conditions, so I nudge the sentiment modestly higher, while remaining short of outright exuberance.
